# Overview

`InferPheno` infers clinical and molecular phenotypes from gene
expression by projecting onto a fixed, unsupervised
[Replicable Axes of Variation (RAV)](https://bioconductor.org/packages/GenomicSuperSignature)
basis and then applying a supervised head trained once and shipped
with the package.

The advantage over task-specific classifiers (CMSclassifier, CMScaller,
expression-based MSI panels, XIST/Y panels) is **cross-platform and
cross-tissue transferability**: because the feature basis is fixed at
projection time and was not estimated from the supervised label, the
head generalizes better to platforms and cohorts unseen during fitting.

# Quick start

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(InferPheno)
library(SummarizedExperiment)

## Which phenotypes can I infer right now?
availablePheno()

## se is a SummarizedExperiment with HGNC-symbol rownames.
res <- inferpheno(se, "msi_status")
res                       # per-sample class + confidence
attr(res, "head_perf")    # head-level out-of-fold performance
```

The result is a data.frame subclass (`inferpheno_result`) with one row
per sample. For binary and multiclass heads it carries a `confidence`
column equal to the maximum class probability; for regression heads
`confidence` is `NA_real_`. The `head_perf` attribute reports the
head's out-of-fold AUC, R^2, or accuracy, depending on the task.

# Reproducing the manuscript figures

Each figure in Oh et al. (2026) is reproduced by a single script under
`benchmark/`, `shift/`, or `atlas/` in the companion repository
`InferPhenoCuration`. See `inst/scripts/reproduce_manuscript.R` for a
top-level driver that calls them in order.
